name: clock-jumped-back
description: Six hours on a 0.85 U/hr profile with boluses from the pump's screen. Three hours ago the pump's clock went back two days with no record of it and no reboot: everything before is stamped two days after everything since, and nothing in the log explains it. No pump is known to do this (only a reset is known to move the clock unrecorded); it stands for a clock lost without a trace, which a reader can find only by a stamp running back. Nothing from before the jump can be dated; the 1.0 U bolus 90 minutes ago is on the clock the pump runs now, which ends two days behind, past a 24-hour trust limit.
